Jasmine / team / Anita — adding our technical summary and suggested questionnaire responses below (high level):

1) BYOK and key custody model
- Hosted API: we support CMK/BYOK via AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure Key Vault. Customer controls key material; Redwood only holds encrypted key references and never has access to plaintext keys when BYOK is enabled. For customers who require zero-operator access, we recommend Dedicated or Private with HSM-backed key wrap.

2) Key rotation & access control
- Rotation: Customers can rotate keys on their KMS side; Redwood tolerates key rotation by supporting key aliasing and rewrap flows. We log key-access events and provide audit entries for key usage (see logs section).

3) Audit logs & SIEM export
- We maintain key-access audit logs for 365 days for Dedicated/Private customers and 90 days for hosted tiers by default. Logs include request timestamps, model, route ID, and the KMS operation ID. We can export logs via S3/Cloud Storage or push to your SIEM via syslog/collector.

4) Cross-region replication & EU data handling
- By default, hosted keys are region-scoped; we do not replicate customer-managed keys across regions without explicit configuration. For EU data residency customers, we can restrict keys and model serving to EU-only regions.

5) HSM-backed option
- For customers needing FIPS 140-2/3 HSMs and separate key envelopes, Redwood Private deploys with HSM integration and can support HSM-on-prem or cloud HSMs.

Attachments included: short answer set for each questionnaire section (I’ll upload to the Drive). Recommended next step: 30-min technical sync with DevOps to walk the KMS endpoints and log delivery format.

Quick note on timeline: we can return the completed questionnaire by Mon (24 May) if the scope is limited to the encryption/KMS section; if they ask for infra hardening specifics we may need an extra 2 business days.

- Marcus Lin
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
